method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md §6.5 manual validation (run_loop.py uses select(), broken on Windows per §6.4). FULL RE-RUN 2026-06-11 against the read-framed description (HCBR-2026-06-11-03 fix: 'Author or interpret', read-side audit cases, 'before writing or reading' closing): all 20 original queries re-measured + 6 new (q21-24 read-side should-trigger incl. the exact FormID-addressing line misdiagnosed in the field report; q25-26 read-shaped should-not near-misses). Empirical step = independent fan-out of 26 fresh-context agents, one per query, each shown a neutral menu of 8 skill descriptions (skypatcher-authoring at C among realistic siblings, NOT flagged as under-test; the form-distribution sibling shown read-framed, matching deployment) + one query, asked which ONE skill to load (or NONE) + reasoning. Anonymized per feedback_skill_trigger_eval_fanout; agents told to judge ONLY the menu, use no tools beyond reading it, and ignore environment skills. Verdicts adjudicated from each agent's REASONING + pick. Menu: A=form-distribution (SPID/KID/CID), B=esp-patching, C=skypatcher-authoring [under test], D=mutagen-reference record-schema, E=crash-diagnostics, F=conflict-resolution, G=papyrus-reference, H=modding-basics. Menu + raw run-record in dev/skill-validation/2026-06-11-read-triggers/ (private). Supersedes the 2026-06-02 run (whose 20 queries are q1-q20 here, all verdicts reconfirmed).

result.notes: All 14 should-trigger picked C — the 10 originals (write-side, reconfirmed) and all 4 new read-side cases: q21 audit-a-mod's-inis-for-an-NPC, q22 the exact filterByNpcs=HearthFires.esm|03005215 line whose FormID form was misdiagnosed from memory in HCBR-2026-06-11-03 (agent cited the Plugin.esp|FormID addressing clause as the reason to load), q23 why-aren't-the-damage-changes-applying, q24 pre-install review-what-it-changes. All 12 should-not routed elsewhere, incl. the two new read-shaped near-misses: q25 (what does this _DISTR.ini do → A: framework beat read-verb) and q26 (read a .psc for NPC health changes → G). Hard originals all held: q20 names SkyPatcher but is install → H; q4/q9 implicit no-name cases still fire. Every manual_predicted_trigger matched the measured verdict.
result.peer_review: Author prediction + 26 independent fresh-context agents (exceeds §6.5's 'one peer reviewer checks 3 random'). Re-run required by PR #42 independent review (stale-eval blocking finding). Aaron may spot-check any query.
result.carry_forward: Re-run on the next release that ships a Windows-compatible eval runner (run_loop.py select() fix), per §6.4.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.method: 2026-07-28 revalidation for issue #294 (all 13 descriptions compressed to the amended section-3.5 200-400 char target): section-6.5 fan-out, one fresh-context sonnet (low effort) agent per query, each shown the full lettered menu of all 13 NEW descriptions (under-test skill unflagged, letter B) plus NONE, asked which ONE to load; one opus adjudicator per skill scored from reasoning per section-6.5 step 4. No fable-model agents. Conductor session: #294 worktree.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes:
Perfect run: recall 14/14 (100%), specificity 12/12 (100%). Thresholds 0.80 / 0.50 both cleared. No misses, no reasoning-vs-pick overrides — every reasoning string matches its pick token.

Recall detail: all 14 true rows picked B, and the reasoning quotes B's own trigger clauses (unlevel encounter zones, disable a placed reference, which subfolder a .ini belongs in, why a patch line isn't applying, audit/review a mod's INI patches). The enumerated trigger list is doing the work directly — rows 6, 7, 10, 21, 23, 24 each cite a specific clause verbatim, i.e. these are description hits not topic guesses. The audit/interpret half (21–24) is as strong as the authoring half (1–10), which is the harder direction and often where distributor skills leak.

Specificity detail: the three near-neighbour distractors all resolved cleanly — SPID spell-to-NPC → E (11), KID keyword-to-items → J (12), SPID _DISTR interpretation → E (25). B's negative-boundary sentence ("This is keywords on ITEMS — keywords on NPCs are SPID…" as mirrored in the sibling descriptions) appears to be holding the three-way distributor split.

Hardest specificity row is 20 ("how do i install skypatcher and its requirements in MO2"): the agent named B explicitly, then rejected it on scope — "Skill B is scoped to authoring/interpreting SkyPatcher INI syntax, not installation/MO2 setup." That is a lexical-lure row (the product name is in the query) declined on the described capability rather than on the keyword, which is the strongest evidence in the set that the description's scope is read, not just pattern-matched.

Residual risk not exercised by this set: no row pits SkyPatcher against biped-slot-reference (find-by-slot vs edit-a-field) or against bulk-record-jobs for a "rebalance every X" phrasing that could read as a bulk deliverable — row 9 ("rebalance every two-handed weapon's swing speed") is the closest and went to B correctly, but only because "runtime ini patch, no plugin" was stated. A future eval round could drop that qualifier to probe the B-vs-D edge. Also untested: SkyPatcher vs a direct ESP override ("just patch it in an esp instead"), where B should NOT trigger. Neither gap affects this verdict.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294.contamination_audit_2026-07-28: 2026-07-28 PR #295 review follow-up (contamination audit): the independent review found adjudicator notes quoting text that exists only in the PRE-compression descriptions. Forensics on the run journal established: (a) judges were shown the NEW menu (the loader agent's journaled return contains it verbatim); (b) 11 of 281 judge rows leaked OLD description text from the agents' own environment skill listing (the installed plugin) into their reasoning; (c) separately, some opus adjudicator notes confabulated 'verbatim quotes' from that same stale environment. All contaminated rows were re-judged with a hardened prompt (explicit stale-environment warning): 15/15 confirmed their original verdicts, except dialogue-authoring q19, whose recorded MISS was itself a contamination artifact and is overturned. Treat quoted description text in the run-1 adjudicator_notes above as unreliable where it does not appear in the shipped description; scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by the hardened re-run. Skill-specific: 'unlevel encounter zones' (q7) and 'which subfolder' (q10) are QUERY tokens the judges restated, not description clauses as the note implies; 'disable a placed reference' (q6) WAS a stale-environment quote — hardened re-run of q6 still picks B on the shipped text (rebalance/no-ESP framing). q15, q20, q26 re-confirmed. All scores unchanged.
